claims.text: Self-RAG trains an arbitrary language model to generate fine-grained self-reflection and customizable inference, using reflection tokens from a critic model added to task examples offline, at far lower training cost than RLHF (per the excerpt of the Self-RAG related-work section).

In Self-RAG, reflection tokens are used at inference to decide the need for retrieval and to self-evaluate generation quality, enabling controllable generation; this excerpt describes the method design and reports no benchmark results.

The ReAct excerpt states that on two interactive decision making benchmarks (ALFWorld and WebShop), ReAct outperforms imitation and reinforcement learning methods by an absolute success rate of 34% and 10% respectively, while being prompted with only one or two in-context examples; the success-rate metric is as stated in the abstract excerpt and the full protocol is not shown.

The ReAct excerpt motivates combining task-oriented actions with verbal reasoning by analogy to human cognition (e.g., tracking progress, handling exceptions, and recognizing when external information is needed); this is motivation, not evaluation evidence.
